summary: H&M delivered strong Q1 report with catastrophic Q2 guidance. Most companies cancelling dividends while Intrum continues both dividends and buybacks. Oil companies moved sharply on OPEC expectations. Retail and property markets under pressure. Chinese fraud case (Luckin Coffee) highlights risks in that market. Coronavirus numbers improving in Europe, but earnings guidance expected to be very poor.
key_takeaways: H&M considered a good long-term hold if price drops to around 100 SEK, especially given their strong negotiating position with landlords
Intrum unique in maintaining dividends and buybacks, signaling confidence despite short-seller attacks
Most companies cancelling dividends to preserve cash during crisis, creating challenges for income-dependent investors
Oil prices volatile on OPEC negotiations but demand remains very weak with global travel restrictions
Real estate and retail sectors face significant pressure as many tenants paying reduced or no rent
